Bignoniaceae.key_tie_breaker: long bivalved capsule + flat winged seeds

Plantaginaceae.key_tie_breaker: Penstemon: 4 fertile stamens + sterile beardtongue/staminode + ordinary capsule

Apiaceae.key_tie_breaker: inferior bicarpellate ovary + schizocarp splitting into two mericarps; Eryngium is a head-forming exception to classic umbels

Papaveraceae.key_tie_breaker: colored latex + caducous 2–3 sepals + many free stamens + syncarpous capsule

Oleaceae.key_tie_breaker: Local split: Fraxinus = odd-pinnate leaves + samara; Forestiera = simple leaves + one-seeded drupe. Family node is opposite/subopposite and exstipulate.
Oleaceae.teaching_caution: Do not teach four petals or exactly two stamens as absolutes; local Fraxinus/Forestiera can be apetalous and Forestiera pubescens can exceed the typical two-stamen pattern.

Onagraceae.key_tie_breaker: Inferior ovary below a hypanthium/floral tube + usually 4-part flower + commonly 4-lobed stigma. Then split classic primrose capsules from former-Gaura hard indehiscent fruits.
teaching_cautions: Do not teach Onagraceae by flower color.
Do not treat radial symmetry or 8 stamens as absolutes.
Do not call every local fruit a dehiscent capsule; sect. Gaura often has hard indehiscent few-seeded capsules.
Oenothera lindheimeri retains its existing user-approved range exception.

Anacardiaceae.taxonomy_note: Source-row count includes synonym/duplicate concepts: Rhus trilobata folds into Rhus aromatica var. aromatica; Toxicodendron rydbergii maps to Toxicodendron radicans subsp. rydbergii.
Anacardiaceae.key_tie_breaker: Woody + alternate exstipulate leaves + resinous tissues + small usually 5-merous flowers + superior ovary + drupe. For local genus split: Rhus usually red hairy terminal drupes; Toxicodendron pale axillary drupes, with aerial rootlets in climbing T. radicans.
teaching_cautions: Do not teach 'leaves of three = poison ivy'; Rhus aromatica also has three leaflets.
Do not use sap contact or crushing as an identification test.
Do not double-count Rhus trilobata as a separate current species under the present POWO/FNA treatment.
Keep Toxicodendron radicans subsp. rydbergii pending dedicated local/range review.
next_actions: rights-safe winged-rachis macro for Rhus copallinum var. lanceolata
local Rhus flower macro showing 5-merous flower and disk
Rhus aromatica vs Toxicodendron radicans comparison card

Cupressaceae.key_tie_breaker: Juniperus = evergreen scale/awl foliage + fleshy berry-like seed cones; Taxodium = deciduous linear foliage on short shoots + woody globose seed cones. Juniper 'berries' are cones, not fruits.
Cupressaceae.joey_comparison: Taxodium mucronatum video extraction retained for family/reproductive morphology study; current POWO maps that name to Taxodium distichum var. mexicanum.
teaching_cautions: Do not call Juniperus fleshy seed cones berries/fruits in the botanical module.
Do not teach Cupressaceae as always evergreen or scale-leaved; Taxodium is a deciduous linear-leaved exception.
Do not keep Taxodium in separate Taxodiaceae in the current learner.
Keep local Taxodium at species level until dedicated infraspecific review.
next_actions: Central Texas Ashe female seed-cone close-up
deep review Juniperus virginiana and Taxodium distichum

Sapindaceae.taxonomy_note: Raw pool includes western-soapberry synonym/typo rows; current POWO accepts Sapindus drummondii, while S. saponaria s.s. remains a separate held range/taxonomy question.
Sapindaceae.key_tie_breaker: Use fruit + leaf arrangement: Acer = opposite + paired samaras; Sapindus = alternate pinnate + translucent drupe-like soapberries; Ungnadia = alternate pinnate + woody 3-valved capsule.
teaching_cautions: Modern Sapindaceae includes Acer; do not rely on older Aceraceae placement.
Do not teach one leaf arrangement or one fruit type as universal.
Do not double-count Sapindus saponaria var./subsp. drummondii separately from S. drummondii.
Exclude cultivated Acer palmatum from native metrics.
Keep S. saponaria sensu stricto on manual taxonomy/range hold.
next_actions: boxelder vs Fraxinus paired/single samara card

Aquifoliaceae.approval_note: Ilex decidua and I. vomitoria are B017 strict-range PASS but still await explicit species approval. Ilex opaca is user-approved only as a labeled lookalike/nursery-trade comparison; target-zone FAIL remains.
Aquifoliaceae.key_tie_breaker: Alternate simple leaves + tiny axillary unisexual flowers + dioecy + superior ovary + red drupe containing several hard pyrenes. Local species split starts with deciduous vs evergreen and leaf margin/texture.
teaching_cautions: Do not teach hollies as always evergreen or always spiny.
Do not identify Ilex by red fruit alone.
Call the fruit a drupe with multiple pyrenes, not a true berry.
Do not promote Ilex opaca into native metrics.
next_actions: local Ilex decidua staminate and pistillate macros

Commelinaceae.taxonomy_note: Three old Commelina erecta infraspecific source rows are duplicate/synonym concepts under the current accepted C. erecta framework.
Commelinaceae.key_tie_breaker: Sheathing jointed monocot herb + 3 sepals/3 petals + superior ovary + capsule. Genus split: Tradescantia 6 fertile hairy stamens; Commelina 3 fertile + 3 staminodes in a folded spathe; Tinantia 6 fertile heteromorphic hairy stamens.
teaching_cautions: Do not teach all members as three equal blue petals.
Do not teach six fertile stamens as universal.
Do not identify vegetative plants from grass-like leaves alone.
Do not split old Commelina erecta variety rows into separate first-pass learner cards.
Keep Tradescantia pedicellata provenance-sensitive because it is a tracked Llano-Uplift endemic.

Berberidaceae.key_tie_breaker: Local Berberis = evergreen prickly shrub + yellow wood + spiny compound leaflets + 6 nectar-bearing petals/6 stamens + anthers opening by two hinged valves + berry. Nandina is the family exception with longitudinal-slit anthers.
teaching_cautions: Do not teach valvate anthers as universal across Berberidaceae.
Do not simplify the local Berberis flower to '6 tepals'; teach petaloid sepals plus 6 true nectar-bearing petals.
Do not count Mahonia synonym rows as separate current taxa.
Do not identify B. swaseyi vs B. trifoliolata by leaflet count alone because hybrids occur in Central Texas.
Exclude Nandina domestica and Berberis aquifolium from project-native metrics.
next_actions: strict-range species deep reviews for B. trifoliolata and B. swaseyi

Orobanchaceae.key_tie_breaker: Green hemiparasites are normal in the family. Use simple exstipulate leaves + bracted spike + fused tubular/bilateral corolla + usually 4 stamens + superior ovary + many-seeded capsule; in Castilleja the bright color is mainly in bracts.
teaching_cautions: Do not teach Orobanchaceae as necessarily leafless or non-green.
Do not call Castilleja colored bracts petals.
Do not require visible host attachment; haustoria are underground.
Do not keep C. purpurea var. lindheimeri as the current accepted name; use C. lindheimeri.
Do not separate the family from Plantaginaceae/Lamiaceae by corolla shape alone.
next_actions: Castilleja capsule and reticulate seed macro
green hemiparasite vs pale holoparasite comparison

Ebenaceae.key_tie_breaker: Alternate simple entire leaves + fused urn/bell-shaped flowers + superior multi-loculed ovary + berry with conspicuous persistent/accrescent calyx. Species split: D. texana pale exfoliating bark/tiny leaves/black hairy fruit vs D. virginiana dark blocky bark/large pointed leaves/orange fruit.
teaching_cautions: Do not make dioecy an absolute D. texana character; authoritative local/broader sources disagree.
Do not identify persimmons from fruit color alone.
Do not confuse the persistent calyx with a separate leaf-like fruit structure.
Keep D. virginiana on strict target-zone review hold despite Texas nativity.
next_actions: local D. texana male/female flower macro pair
strict target-zone review for D. virginiana
reconcile D. texana sex-system source conflict

Pteridaceae.key_tie_breaker: Read the frond, then flip it over: marginal/submarginal sori + no true indusium + recurved margin acting as a false indusium. Local xeric members add distinctive hairs/scales and rachis architecture.
teaching_cautions: False indusium is rolled blade tissue, not a separate membrane.
Not every Pteridaceae has the same marginal-sorus pattern.
Do not assume Central Texas ferns require wet forest conditions.
Do not make drought-curling a universal family trait.
Preserve familiar Cheilanthes/Pellaea names in field context while recording current POWO Hemionitis taxonomy.

Platanaceae.key_tie_breaker: Mottled exfoliating bark + alternate palmately lobed stipulate leaves + petiole base hiding the axillary bud + encircling stipule scar + spherical fruiting head of many achenes.
teaching_cautions: Do not identify Platanus from mottled bark alone.
Do not call the whole spherical head one fruit; it contains many achenes.
Do not confuse Platanus with Acer: Platanus leaves are alternate, Acer leaves opposite.
Do not confuse Platanus with Liquidambar: sycamore fruit heads are fuzzy achene heads, not hard spiny capsule balls.
next_actions: sheathing stipule and annular scar macro
fruiting head breaking into individual hairy achenes

Rubiaceae.key_tie_breaker: Opposite/whorled simple leaves + interpetiolar stipules + fused mostly radial corolla + inferior ovary. Galium is the stipule trick: leaf-like stipules help form the apparent whorl.
teaching_cautions: Do not use opposite leaves alone.
Do not assume stipules always look like small separate flaps.
Do not teach one Rubiaceae fruit type.
Exclude Galium aparine from native metrics under current POWO treatment.
Do not use square stems alone against Lamiaceae/Verbenaceae.
next_actions: individual buttonbush flower showing inferior ovary
local G. aparine/G. texense/G. virgatum comparison

Sapotaceae.stale_audit_fix: Old action referenced Sideroxylon celastrinum; live project pool contains Sideroxylon lanuginosum, so the family package was corrected to the actual anchor.
Sapotaceae.key_tie_breaker: Woody plant + alternate entire leaves + sticky/milky latex + small axillary fascicles + radial fused corolla with fertile stamens opposite the lobes and petaloid staminodes alternating between them + fleshy berry with a hard glossy seed.
teaching_cautions: Do not make thorns mandatory; Sideroxylon lanuginosum can be armed or unarmed.
Do not damage healthy plants solely to prove latex.
Do not identify from black fruit alone.
Do not assume several seeds in local S. lanuginosum fruit; Williamson material commonly has one large seed.
Keep local S. lanuginosum at species level until the albicans/oblongifolium subspecies conflict is reconciled.
next_actions: live flower macro separating stamens and staminodes

Rosaceae.taxonomy_note: Malus ioensis var. texana source row maps to accepted Malus ioensis under current POWO; Prunus serotina var. eximia remains an accepted Texas-native variety under current POWO.
Rosaceae.key_tie_breaker: Usually stipules + hypanthium + 5-part radial flower + many stamens, then determine fruit architecture: Prunus drupe; Rubus aggregate drupelets; Geum aggregate achenes; Malus/Crataegus pome.
teaching_cautions: Do not reduce Rosaceae to Prunus or to five petals and many stamens.
Do not assume one ovary position across the family.
Do not assume stipules remain conspicuous in every woody taxon.
Do not call Rubus fruit one berry; it is an aggregate of drupelets.
Keep Malus and uncurated Crataegus/Prunus source concepts on their species/range review tracks.
Rosaceae.phase_note: This Rosaceae package completes the substantial/authoritative family-backfill phase; remaining family work is Joey-sufficient verification and visual polish.

Lamiaceae.key_tie_breaker: Common pattern: opposite exstipulate leaves + often quadrangular aromatic stem + tubular/bilabiate flower + superior deeply 4-lobed ovary/gynobasic style + 4 nutlets. Important local exceptions: Salvia has 2 fertile stamens, Scutellaria has a calyx scutellum, Callicarpa is actinomorphic and drupaceous.
teaching_cautions: Square stems are common, not mandatory.
Aromatic foliage is common, not mandatory.
Bilabiate flowers are common, not universal.
Four dry nutlets are common, not universal; Callicarpa is drupaceous.
Four stamens are not universal; Salvia has two fertile stamens.

Verbenaceae.key_tie_breaker: Opposite exstipulate leaves + indeterminate racemose/spicate/capitate inflorescence + tubular flower + superior ovary with terminal style + genus-specific dry schizocarp or drupaceous fruit. Do not use square stems alone against Lamiaceae.
teaching_cautions: Square stems and aromatic foliage overlap strongly with Lamiaceae.
Terminal style versus gynobasic style is a strong common-pattern distinction, not an absolute across all Lamiaceae.
Verbenaceae fruit is diverse: Verbena/Glandularia 4 mericarps, Phyla 2-part fruit, Lantana drupe.
Retain introduced/cultivated comparison rows but exclude them from native metrics.
non_native_or_comparison_rows: Lantana strigocamara / current POWO Lantana × strigocamara

Asteraceae.key_tie_breaker: Capitulum surrounded by an involucre of phyllaries + individual florets on a common receptacle + usually 5 fused anthers around the style + inferior 1-ovule ovary + cypsela with pappus or pappus reduced/absent.
teaching_cautions: Ray florets are flowers, not petals.
Ray florets may be fertile, sterile or neuter.
Disk florets are not always bisexual/fertile; Silphium is a local counterexample.
Pappus form is highly variable and may be absent.
Use cypsela as the preferred fruit term while recognizing older 'achene' usage.

Fabaceae.key_tie_breaker: Usually alternate stipulate leaves with pulvini + one superior carpel/one locule + a legume or modified legume fruit. Flower architecture may be papilionoid, caesalpinioid-like, or mimosoid.
Fabaceae.taxonomy_update: Use the modern six-subfamily Leguminosae/Fabaceae framework. Traditional Mimosoideae is the mimosoid clade nested within Caesalpinioideae; retain 'mimosoid' only as a useful morphology/clade term.
teaching_cautions: Do not require a classic pea flower.
Do not require a dehiscent two-valved pod.
Do not require pinnately compound leaves.
Do not require obvious stipules.
Do not uproot plants to look for nitrogen-fixing nodules.
Do not present Papilionoideae/Caesalpinioideae/Mimosoideae as the modern three formal subfamilies.
Fabaceae.sheet_health_note: Resolved 2026-10-03: Master Plant Pool A:Z formula spill restored; keyed overrides + family-order map installed; 0 formula/override/map mismatches.

Malvaceae.key_tie_breaker: For the local Malvoideae lesson: alternate stipulate leaves + stellate hairs + superior ovary + many stamens commonly fused into a staminal column. Preserve broad-family variation so the Hibiscus-type flower is not treated as universal.
teaching_cautions: Do not require an epicalyx.
Do not require a staminal column across all broad Malvaceae.
Do not require spreading Hibiscus-like petals.
Malvaviscus provides a fleshy segmented-fruit exception.

Apocynaceae.key_tie_breaker: Broad family: common latex + simple usually opposite/whorled exstipulate leaves + fused 5-lobed corolla + five stamens + superior two-carpel gynoecium. Local milkweed-side confirmation: corona + gynostegium + pollinia/pollinarium + follicle/comose seed.
Apocynaceae.taxonomy_note: Live source row Matelea biflora is reconciled to canonical Chthamalia biflora; do not duplicate it.
Apocynaceae.breadth_note: No non-Asclepiadoideae local anchor is currently present in the live project pool.
teaching_cautions: Do not define all Apocynaceae by a milkweed corona.
Do not require pollinia/pollinaria across the broad family.
Do not require paired follicles across the broad family.
Do not use latex alone as a family ID.

Cactaceae.key_tie_breaker: Find an areole first; then read stem segmentation/ribs/tubercles, spines or glochids, flower position, inferior ovary and berry-like fruit.
Cactaceae.taxonomy_note: O. lindheimeri is a synonym of accepted O. engelmannii var. lindheimeri. Source-row O. senilis remaps to accepted O. orbiculata but remains HOLD pending a clean current-concept target-zone package. O. phaeacantha remains HOLD; historical O. phaeacantha var. major records cannot be counted because current Kew places var. major under O. gilvescens.
next_actions: use installed O. engelmannii var. lindheimeri vs O. macrorhiza comparison
revisit O. orbiculata and O. phaeacantha only when current-taxonomy exact-county evidence closes the HOLD

Asparagaceae.key_tie_breaker: Broad Asparagaceae is heterogeneous; for the local Yucca module start with rosette/trunk + fibrous true leaves and leaf armature, then 3+3 tepals, 6 stamens and 3-carpellate fruit.
Asparagaceae.taxonomy_note: Yucca treculiana is accepted by current Kew; live Yucca treculeana spelling is flagged for source-row reconciliation rather than duplicated.

Aristolochiaceae.key_tie_breaker: Alternate simple often cordate leaves + one fused petaloid perianth/calyx tube with no ordinary corolla + inferior ovary + gynostemium/anthers on stylar column + many-seeded capsule.

Ericaceae.key_tie_breaker: Alternate/spiral exstipulate leaves + fused urn/bell/tubular corolla + 5–10 stamens with commonly poricidal anthers; check ovary position and fruit because both vary across the family.

Euphorbiaceae.key_tie_breaker: Do not start with latex. Confirm tiny unisexual flowers plus a superior usually 3-carpellate ovary/3-part capsule, then choose a genus door: Euphorbia cyathium; Croton stellate/lepidote hairs; Acalypha pistillate bracts; Tragia/Cnidoscolus stinging hairs; Stillingia spike + gynobase.
teaching_cautions: Cyathia diagnose Euphorbia, not Euphorbiaceae as a whole.
Latex is a clue, not a family requirement.
Stinging hairs occur in Tragia and Cnidoscolus and can mimic Urticaceae.
Chamaesyce is retained as source-pool provenance but should be reconciled through the modern Euphorbia lane.
Do not promote concurrent Euphorbia, Croton, Acalypha or Tragia species from the family module.

Cyperaceae.key_tie_breaker: one flower under one scale → one-seeded nutlet; Carex adds perigynium

Boraginaceae.taxonomy_note: Broad POWO Boraginaceae includes former Hydrophyllaceae in this learner.
Boraginaceae.key_tie_breaker: choose classic four-nutlet vs hydrophylloid capsule vs heliotrope vs woody Ehretia door

Solanaceae.key_tie_breaker: fused 5-part flower + superior many-ovuled ovary → berry/capsule; genus split by anther/calyx/fruit

Amaranthaceae.key_tie_breaker: tiny papery/bracteate flowers + usually one-seeded fruit

Polygonaceae.key_tie_breaker: ocrea + one-seeded angled nut; Eriogonum exception

Caryophyllaceae.key_tie_breaker: opposite/swollen node + distinct sepals/free petals + capsule

Plumbaginaceae.key_tie_breaker: persistent tubular calyx + stamens opposite petals + one ovule

Tamaricaceae.key_tie_breaker: scale leaves + flower racemes + tufted seeds

Cleomaceae.key_tie_breaker: glandular 3-foliolate habit + 4 petals + many exserted stamens + long capsule
Cleomaceae.taxonomy_note: Current Kew: Polanisia dodecandra → Cleome dodecandra; P. dodecandra subsp. trachysperma → Cleome trachysperma.

Gentianaceae.key_tie_breaker: opposite exstipulate leaves + fused corolla + superior many-ovuled ovary + many-seeded capsule
Gentianaceae.taxonomy_note: Centaurium beyrichii/calycosum/texense are source-name provenance for current Zeltnera concepts; Centaurium tenuiflorum remains accepted; Eustoma exaltatum subsp. russellianum reconciles to E. russellianum.

Loganiaceae.key_tie_breaker: opposite leaves + stipule/interpetiolar-line clues + superior usually 2-locular ovary + local capsule architecture
Loganiaceae.taxonomy_note: Current learner keeps Gelsemium in Gelsemiaceae rather than older broad Loganiaceae.

Gelsemiaceae.key_tie_breaker: woody twining yellow jessamine + 4-segment septicidal capsule + unilaterally winged seed
Gelsemiaceae.taxonomy_note: Gelsemium is separated from older broad Loganiaceae under the current learner classification.

Rhamnaceae.key_tie_breaker: nectar disc/hypanthium + stamens opposite petals; then capsule-vs-drupe and armature/venation
Rhamnaceae.taxonomy_note: Source Ziziphus obtusifolia is provenance for current Condaliopsis obtusifolia and should not be double-counted.

Moraceae.key_tie_breaker: woody + milky latex + minute unisexual flower clusters + fleshy multiple fruit
Moraceae.teaching_caution: Morus alba is an introduced comparison, not a native family anchor.

Urticaceae.key_tie_breaker: tiny green flowers + inflexed/explosive stamens + one basal ovule → achene; stinging hairs not universal
Urticaceae.teaching_caution: Boehmeria and Parietaria are non-stinging project members.
